This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Puneeth K.N., who is husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 and son of petitioner No.3, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 19-11-2023, between 4.00 to 4.10 p.m., the deceased Puneeth K.N., after finishing his duty at Tiptur was returning to his village by riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-13- EE-0829, from Tiptur to Anathi village, Bagur Hobli, C.R. Patna Taluk,

No.KA-06-HN-0739 rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner,
without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Channarayapatna Government Hospital for treatment,
wherein the doctors examined him and declared as brought dead.
Earlier to the accident the deceased was working as driver cum conductor in KSRTC and was earning a salary of Rs.35,474/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Nuggehalli Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 19-11-2023, between 4.00 to 4.10 p.m.,
when the deceased Puneeth K.N., was returning to his village, by riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.

No.KA-13-EE-0829, from Tiptur to Anathi village, at that time near K. Thimmalapura Gate, on Channarayapatna-Tiptur road, the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased has fell down on the road, sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to said injuries on the way to Channarayapatna Government Hospital.
Further it is contended that,
earlier

11. In order to prove her case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 10 and 25, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the deceased from opposite direction.
Due to said impact the deceased Puneeth K.N. has sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to said injuries on the way to hospital.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.25, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 and dashing the same to oncoming motorcycle of the deceased.

13. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-HN-0739 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondents No.1 and 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and has taken specific defence that, at the time of accident the deceased was riding the Shruthi K C vs Nagaraju on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192429579/
5 motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EE- 0829 in a rash and negligent manner and he had suffered self accident.
Further it is contended that, the alleged insured vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

Though the respondent No.2 has summoned and examined the investigation officer who has conducted the investigation in the case and foisted the charge-sheet against the accused/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HN-0739 nothing worth has been brought out in his evidence which goes to show that, the accident in question is a self accident and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HN-0739 has been falsely implicated in the case by the petitioners.

The R.W.1 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, it is revealed in the investigation that, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HN-0739 the accident in question has taken place and hence, he has filed charge- sheet against the said rider.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.2, who is the representative/Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that,
the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and it has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 and dashing the same to oncoming motorcycle of the deceased.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 15 feet wide on Tiptur-Channarayapatna road, near K. Thimmalapura Gate, Bagur Hobli, Channarayapatna Taluk, Hassan District, in between the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-EE-0829 of the deceased.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.10 and 23 Motor Vehicle Accident reports, the accident has not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.25 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 and dashing the said vehicle to the motorcycle of the deceased and the deceased has succumbed to fatal injuries sustained in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 in the said accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Puneeth K.N., in the said accident and the cause of his death.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

21. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
22. The compensation towards loss of dependency:
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the deceased.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
23. Age and income of the deceased: The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 35 years.

To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card and driving licence of deceased Puneeth K.N., which are marked as Ex.P.16 and 17, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 24-03-1989.
Admittedly, the accident has occurred on 19-11-2023.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was 35 years.
It is averred in the petition that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as driver cum conductor in KSRTC and was earning a salary of Rs.35,474/- per month.

To substantiate the same, they have produced the salary slips for the month of October-2023 and November-2023, Employee Identity card and bank account statement of the deceased, which Shruthi K C vs Nagaraju on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192429579/
8 are marked as Ex.P.11, 12, 19 and 24.
The said documents are clear evident that, prior to accident the deceased was working as driver cum conductor in KSRTC and he was drawing gross salary of Rs.35,474/- per month.
After deducting profession tax of Rs.200/- per month, the net salary of the deceased is considered at Rs.35,274/-.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, with respect to avocation and income of the deceased.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners and hold that,
as on the date of death the monthly income of the deceased was Rs.35,274/-, which comes to Rs.4,23,288/- per annum.
24.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are also entitled for future prospects of the deceased, though he was not a permanent employee as on the date of death.

sentences.text: In the present case, since the deceased was aged about 35 years and was a permanent employee, the future prospects would be 50% of his actual income, which comes to Rs.2,11,644/- per annum.

If this income is added to the actual income, then it comes to Rs.6,34,932/- per annum.
25. The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier: The family of the deceased consist of 3 persons i.e., petitioners No.1 to 3.
The total number of the dependents of the deceased are three.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 1/3rd of the total income, which comes to Rs.2,11,644/-.
After deducting 1/3rd out of total income, towards the personal expenses of deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.4,23,288/-.
26. As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 35 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 16.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.2, who is the representative/Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that,
the offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and it has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.25 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 and dashing the said vehicle to the motorcycle of the deceased and the deceased has succumbed to fatal injuries sustained in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the rider or the owner of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HN-0739 in the said accident, rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Puneeth K.N., in the said accident and the cause of his death.
Further, the Ex.P.6 Post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Puneeth K.N. has died due to severe head injury sustained in road traffic accident.
There is absolutely no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the deceased.

the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the deceased.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, with respect to avocation and income of the deceased.
As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are also entitled for future prospects of the deceased, though he was not a permanent employee as on the date of death.
In the present case, since the deceased was aged about 35 years and was a permanent employee, the future prospects would be 50% of his actual income, which comes to Rs.2,11,644/- per annum.
